To request an increase, submit a request through the AWS Support limit increase form and select **Amazon Bedrock** as the service. In your request, specify:\\n\\n* The endpoint (`bedrock-mantle`).\\n* The Region.\\n* The model.\\n* The quota name (input TPM or output TPM) and the value you are requesting.\\n\\nYou can request increases to input-tokens-per-minute and output-tokens-per-minute for the same model in a single support case. Approval depends on whether your existing usage justifies the increase, so include recent usage information from CloudWatch or the Service Quotas console with your request\",\"url\":\"https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/quotas-mantle.html\"},{\"rank_order\":3,\"title\":\"How do I troubleshoot the \\\"ThrottlingException\\\" error when I use Amazon Bedrock on-demand resources?\",\"context\":\"### Request a quota increase\\n\\nNew AWS accounts might have lower initial quotas than the default quotas. Specific models have non-adjustable fixed quotas. If your workload traffic exceeds your account's on-demand quotas, then contact [AWS Support](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/awssupport/latest/user/case-management.html#creating-a-support-case) or your account manager to [request a quota increase](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/quotas-increase.html). AWS might adjust default quotas based on usage patterns or service requirements.\\n\\nInclude the following information in your request:\\n\\n* The name of the quota to increase\\n* The model ID\\n* The Region for the quota increase\\n* A brief explanation of your use case\\n* Your projected usage, including steady and peak tokens and requests per minute, and average input and output tokens per request\",\"url\":\"https://repost.aws/knowledge-center/bedrock-throttling-error\"},{\"rank_order\":4,\"title\":\"How do I troubleshoot InvokeModel API errors in Amazon Bedrock?\",\"context\":\"### Throttling error\u00a0\\n\\nIf your requests exceed the account quotas or rate limits for the model, then you receive an error similar to one of the following:\u00a0\\n\\n\\\"An error occurred (ThrottlingException) when calling the InvokeModel operation: Too many requests, please wait before trying again.\\\"\u00a0\\n\\n\\\"An error occurred (ThrottlingException) when calling the InvokeModel operation: Too many tokens, please wait before trying again.\\\"\u00a0\\n\\nThis is an HTTP 429 error. To resolve this issue, see [How do I troubleshoot the \\\"ThrottlingException\\\" error when I use Amazon Bedrock on-demand resources?](https://How do I troubleshoot the \\\"ThrottlingException\\\" error when I use Amazon Bedrock on-demand resources)\",\"url\":\"https://repost.aws/knowledge-center/bedrock-invokemodel-api-error\"},{\"rank_order\":5,\"title\":\"Scaling and throughput best practices\",\"context\":\"## Ramping up throughput\\n\\nOn-demand capacity can vary by model, Region, and time. Not all requests within a quota are guaranteed to succeed during periods of high demand, so ramp gradually when launching a workload, changing models or Regions, or making a large traffic increase. This is especially important for `bedrock-mantle` models that do not have a published per-account quota.\\n\\n### Recommended ramp-up procedure\\n\\n1. Estimate the target token rate and concurrency for each endpoint, model, and Region. For `bedrock-mantle`, track input and output tokens separately and include the requested `max_tokens` value in the input-token admission estimate.\\n2. Begin at a known stable baseline below the target. If you do not have a baseline, start with a small representative load instead of sending the full target volume.\\n3. Hold each level long enough to observe request success, 429/503/529 errors, latency percentiles, token consumption, concurrency, and queue depth.\\n4. Increase one controlled step at a time. Change only one major load dimension at a time so that you can identify the cause of a regression.\\n5. If throttling, capacity errors, or latency rise beyond your threshold, pause the ramp, honor any `Retry-After` header, and return to the last stable level.\\n6. Continue until you reach the target, and repeat the validation for every model and Region that will receive production traffic.\\n\\nChoose the step size and observation period from your workload's latency and traffic pattern. Do not use RPM as the only control signal: request token sizes and response lengths can change capacity consumption substantially even when RPM stays constant.\\n\\nFor `bedrock-mantle` quota increases, follow Requesting a quota increase. For `bedrock-runtime`, follow Requesting a quota increase\",\"url\":\"https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/scaling-throughput-best-practices.html\"}]}}"}]}], "label": "Look up Bedrock quota increase documentation"}

{"id": "3c1f66f8-288c-43e4-bbec-60da03ab350e", "role": "assistant", "content": [{"text": "Here's how to raise the quota, based on the current Bedrock documentation.

## 1. Find the quota that's being hit
The error text tells you which limit it is:
- "Too many requests" means requests per minute (RPM).
- "Too many tokens" means tokens per minute (TPM).

Quotas are per model, per Region, and per endpoint. Note the model ID, the Region, and whether you call the model directly (on-demand) or through a cross-Region inference profile.

## 2. Request the increase
- **If the quota is adjustable (Adjustable = Yes in Service Quotas):** Open Service Quotas, choose Amazon Bedrock, find the quota for your model and Region, and choose **Request increase**.
- **For token quotas:** Request an increase on **Cross-Region InvokeModel tokens per minute for `<model>`**. Support will then offer to raise the on-demand TPM and the Cross-Model Max Tokens Per Day quotas at the same time.
- **If the quota isn't adjustable, or Service Quotas doesn't offer an increase:** Open an AWS Support case, or contact your account manager. This is also the route for `bedrock-mantle` endpoint quotas.

Include these details in the request:
- Quota name, model ID, and Region.
- Your use case.
- Projected steady and peak RPM and TPM.
- Average input and output tokens per request.
- Recent usage from CloudWatch or Service Quotas. AWS says priority goes to customers who are already consuming their current allocation, so a request can be denied if your usage doesn't justify it.

## Caveats
- **Model lifecycle:** Increases aren't granted for models that are Legacy or scheduled for retirement. Consider moving to the successor model.
- **New accounts:** These often have lower default quotas, and some models have fixed quotas that can't be raised.
- **Access:** A quota increase doesn't grant access to a model. Model access has to be enabled separately.

## Reducing throttling while you wait
- Retry with exponential backoff and jitter, and honor any `Retry-After` header.
- Ramp traffic up gradually. Capacity can vary by model, Region, and time, and staying under your quota doesn't guarantee success during high demand.
- Use a cross-Region inference profile, which can spread load across Regions.
- Lower `max_tokens` to what you actually need, because it counts toward token quota consumption.

I can check your current Bedrock quotas and recent throttling metrics in the account if you tell me the model and Region. If you also want to know why the throttling started, that's a root-cause question and I can open a tracked investigation for it.

Sources:
- https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/quotas-runtime.html
- https://repost.aws/knowledge-center/bedrock-throttling-error
- https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/scaling-throughput-best-practices.html", "type": "text"}], "created_at": null}
